Disclosure to Promote the Right To Information 

Whereas the Parliament of India has set out to provide a practical regime of right to 
information for citizens to secure access to information under the control of public authorities, 
in order to promote transparency and accountability in the working of every public authority, 
and whereas the attached publication of the Bureau of Indian Standards is of particular interest 
to the public, particularly disadvantaged communities and those engaged in the pursuit of 
education and knowledge, the attached public safety standard is made available to promote the 
timely dissemination of this information in an accurate manner to the public.

IS : 292 - 1983 

Indian Standard 

SPECIFICATION FOR 
LEADED BRASS INGOTS AND CASTINGS 



(Second Revision) 



0. FOREWORD 

0.1 This Indian Standard ( Sorond Revision ) was ndoptod by tlie Indian 
Standards Institution on 30 November 1983, after tlie draft finalized by 
the (Copper and Copper Alloys Sectional Conunittee had bc^en apj^roved 
by the Structural and Metals Division Councij. 

0.2 This standard was fust published in 1951 and subsefjuently revised 
in 1961. In this revision only Gra(U^ I and Grade 3 liave been retained 
with certain modifications in chennc al composition and designated as 
LCH 1 and LCB 2 respectively. Clauses for chemical composition, size 
and shaj)e and sampling and criteria for conlbrmity have idso been 
modified. 

0.3 The two i^rades of jjra.ss specified in this standard are commonly used 
in the brass industry having copper and zinc as their main constituents 
with a small quantity of lead added to improve pressme-tiglitness and 
niachinability. These are basically a brasses having dispersed consti- 
tuents of lead or some impurities within permiysible limit mentioned in 
the standard in a matrix. Field of applicability for sand cast brasses 
designated in this standard as LCB 1 and LGH 2 pertains to small size 
valves, cocks, plumbing fittings and for general engineering applications 
having tensile strength of about 180 MPa and about 12 percent elongation 
(for information only ). 

0.4 For the purpose of deciding wliedier a particular requirement of this 
standard is complied with, the final value, observed or calculated, 
expressing the result of a test or analysis, shall be rounded off in 
accordance with IS : 2-1960*. The number of significant places 
retained in the rounded oil value should be the same as that of the 
specified value in this standard. 

•Ruins lor rounding off numerical values ( revised ).

1. SCOPE 

l.I This standard covers the requirements for two grades of leaded brass 
ingots and casting designated as LCB 1 and LGB 2. 

2. SUPPLY OF MATERIAL 

2.1 General requirements relating to the supply of material are laid down 
in IS : 1387-1967*.

3.1 The material shall have the chemical composition as given in

•The chemical analysis for aluminium is not required if the supplier undertakes and

the table. 



3.2 The chemical composition shall be determined either by the method 
specified in LS : 3685-1966f or any other established instrumental/ 
chemical method. In case of dispute, the procedure specified in the 
latest edition of IS : 3685| for chemical analysis shall be the referee 
method. 

3.3 The manufacturer shall, when required, supply free of charge a copy 
of his works analysis of the material. Works analysis is defined as the 
routine analysis by the manufacturer in order to control the quality of 
the material. 



♦General requirements for the supply of metallurgical mattrials {first revision ). 
fMethods of chemical analysis of brasses. 



IS ! 292 - 1983 

4. PRESSURE TEST 

4.1 If the purchaser requires castings to be tested for pressure this shall 
be stated in the enquiry and order. The number of tests, the nature of 
the test, the test pressure and the testing fluid shall be subject to agree- 
ment between the supplier and the purchaser, 

5. FREEDOM FROM DEFECTS 

5.1 Ingots -— The ingots shall be of uniform quality and reasonably free 
from slag, dross and other harmful contaminations. 

5.2 Castings — The castings shall be clean, and free from harmful 
defects such as, blow-holes and gas cavities. Castings shall not be repaired 
unless permission in writing has been obtained previously from the 
purchaser or his representative. 

6. SIZE AND SHAPE 

6.1 Shape and size of ingots shall be as agreed to between the supplier 
and the purchaser. 

6.2 The dimensions of the casting shall be in accordance with the 
drawing. All surfaces marked for machining shall have sufficient 
allowance for that purpose but this shall not be too excessive resulting 
in more machining, and unnecessary increase in the mass of the casting. 

7. MARKING 

7.1 The name or trade-mark of the manufacturer and the cast number 
and grade of the material shall be cast or otherwise legibly marked by 
stamping on each ingot or casting, by which the manufacturer and the 
grade of the material may be identified. In the case of small castings 
where it is difficult to cast on or stamp all the details, the marking shall 
be as agreed to between the purchaser and the supplier. 

7.1.1 The product may also be marked with Standard Mark. 



7.1.2 The use of the Standard Mark is governed by the provisions of the Bureau 
of Indian Standards Act, 1 986 and the Rules and Regulations made thereunder. 
The details of conditions under which the licence for the use of Standard Mark 
may be granted to manufactures or producers may be obtained from the Bureau 
of Indian Standards. 



IS : 292 - 1983 

8. SAMPLING AND CRITERIA FOR CONFORMITY 

8.0 Unless otherwise decided by mutual agreement of the purchaser and 
the suppher, the following sampling procedure and criteria for conformity 
shall hold good. 

8.1 Lot — In any consignment, ingots/castings of the same grade ( see 
Table 1 ) manufactured ai the same place shall be grouped together to 
constitute a lot. 

8.2 Sampling for Chemical Analysis — One sample shall be taken 
and analysed from each cast of 1 000 kg or part thereof of the ingots/ 
castings. However, in case more frequent chemical analysis is required, 
the same shall be agreed to between the supplier and the purchaser. The 
sampling for chemical analysis shall be taken by drilling or sawing in 
such a manner as to be representative of the entire cross section. 
Drillings and sawings from ingots/castings shall be obtained in a(cordance 
with the appropriate procedure specified in IS : 1817-1961*. 

8.3 Criteria of Conformity — If the test result of chemical analysis as 
obtained for each of the constituent satisfy the corresponding require- 
ments, the lot shall be considered as conforming to the cliemical 
requirement of the specification. 

8.4 Retcst — If the sample drawn for cliemical analysis fails to meet 
the requirements stipulated in the standard, two more tests shall be 
conducted on the same sample in order to confirm that the analysis has 
been done properly. If both the tejt results satisfy the j(?lfViuit require- 
ments, the lot shall be accepted; and if either of the retest fidls, the lot 
represented shall be deemed as not complying with tlie standard. 

9. INFORMATION TO BE GIVEN BY THE PURCHASER 

9.1 This standard contains a number of clauses in which the purchaser 
is allowed to exercise an option. I'he list of information to be given by 
the purchaser in respect to these clauses is given in Appendix A. 



♦Methods of sampling non-ferrous metals for chemical analysis

A PPENDIX A 

( Clause 9.1 ) 

INFORMATION TO BE GIVEN BY THE PURCHASER 

A-1. Whether the purchaser wishes to inspect the material at the supplier's 
works ( see 2 and IS : 1387-1967* ). 

A-2. The alloy grade required. 

A-3. Whether information is required concerning the works analysis. 

A-4, Detailed drawings of castings. 

A-5. In the case of ingots, whether purchaser prefers any special size, 
shape and mass of the ingots. 

A-6. Marking details.
